widgets.value:
### OAuth client
The values ported from agentic-workspace are the **Workspace MCP** *Desktop app* client in the `crispal` Google Cloud project. Desktop clients accept any `localhost` redirect, which is what this server's callback uses — a Web client would need its exact callback URL registered in Google Cloud first.

The secret is stored in the zero-knowledge secret store, never in plain config.

fields.label: OAuth client ID
fields.description: Not a credential on its own — also visible in this app's Settings.

fields.label: OAuth client secret
fields.description: Leave blank to keep the secret already saved.

widgets.value: ### Authorizing a Google account A saved OAuth client is not consent — grant it below. Connect Google Account → Opens in a new tab and starts a fresh Google consent flow for the configured account. The callback lands on this server's own `/oauth2callback`, so the browser completing it must be able to reach that port. Use this to (re)authorize, or to recover from an expired/revoked token — no agent needed. If that tab lands on a connection error instead, see **Consent redirect landed on a dead tab?** below. **Or import an existing token** — if this account was already authorized in agentic-workspace, copy its `.json` from that host's `.tmp/google_workspace_mcp_credentials/` and POST it to `/api/apps/google-workspace-mcp/credentials` with `{"email": "…", "credentials": {…}}`. No consent screen, no browser. Tokens live in `$AW_WORKSPACE_HOME/data/google-workspace-mcp/credentials/` and survive an app reinstall.

widgets.title: Consent redirect landed on a dead tab?

widgets.value: The OAuth client is a Google **Desktop app** client, so Google only allows redirecting to `localhost` — from your browser that means *your own machine*, not this container. If clicking Connect above ends on a tab that fails to load, the authorization code is still sitting in that tab's address bar. Copy the whole URL and paste it here to finish signing in.

fields.label: Redirect URL from the dead tab
fields.description: Host and port are ignored — only the code/state query string matters.

widgets.value:
### Server
`workspace-mcp` runs in its own private venv — never the workspace's shared one, whose `starlette`/`cryptography`/`mcp` versions it would otherwise upgrade under every other Python MCP server. Reinstall it after changing `pin_version` in Settings.
